title: Electric field due to point charges; field lines
topicTitle: Electric field due to point charges; field lines
notes: **Electric field intensity.** The field at a point is the force per unit positive test charge placed there: E = F/q₀ = (1/4πε₀)q/r² for a point charge, directed away from a positive charge.
**Field lines.** These imaginary lines are drawn so that the tangent at any point gives the field direction and their density shows field strength.
**Field line rules.** Lines start on positive charges and end on negative ones, never cross each other, and never form closed loops in electrostatics.
**Uniform field.** Between two parallel oppositely charged plates the field is uniform (E = V/d), so a charge experiences the same force everywhere between the plates.
**Superposition.** The total field from several charges is the vector sum of their individual fields — the same principle that gives the net force.
